about: The key set endpoints (core §2.12.2; forward-secrecy FS-H4, CORE-E5, CORE-E7, G1). POST /agents/{aid}/keys, signed for "keys" by the agent itself, takes {keys, prev_seq}: keys is the signed key set in base64url, decoded strictly (a padded or standard-alphabet spelling, or the wire-2 member keyset, is 400 bad_request), and prev_seq, required, is the seq of the last set the publisher signed before it. A hub that holds a set with a higher seq than prev_seq refuses it 409 keys_rollback and names that seq (stored_seq), and so does a set whose seq is not above the stored one; the stored set sent again is unchanged whatever its prev_seq. A set that does not verify for the agent, or breaks the mailbox key rule (SSR-W9), is 400 bad_request saying why. GET /agents/{aid}/keys answers {aid, keys, kel}, both base64url, or 404: unknown_aid for an AID not registered here, not_found for an agent with no key set. /register with enc_keys (base64url) needs prev_seq too, and refuses a set that does not follow the stored one with 409 keys_rollback before it writes anything.
